vulnerability.title: Undici header normalization is quadratic on long internal whitespace runs, giving Headers.set()/append() a ReDoS

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.19.1 (984d53ba) headerValueNormalize() no longer applies a trailing regex; it trims with an explicit charAt loop and only the anchored leading regex remains

severity.numeric_level_rationale: CNA, NVD Primary, NVD Secondary and GHSA/OSV all publish CVSS 3.1 7.5 High with the same vector; the CWE differs but the score does not. For classification, CWE-1333 (Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity) is the precise class; the CNA record and OSV carry CWE-20 instead.
severity.source: GitHub_M CNA and nvd@nist.gov (NVD Primary), both CVSS 3.1 7.5 High
severity.ghsa_label_note: GHSA/OSV labels the issue HIGH and publishes the same CVSS 3.1 vector.

vulnerability.category_l2: Inefficient regular expression: header value normalization rescans trailing/embedded whitespace at every offset

critical_operation.description: headerValueNormalize() trims a header value with a global regular expression whose second alternative is anchored only at the end. For a value that contains a long run of tabs/CR/LF followed by a non-whitespace byte, the engine retries that alternative at every starting offset and scans to the end each time, so the cost is quadratic in the length of the run. Headers.append() (line 211) and Headers.set() (line 348) call this function on the caller-supplied ByteString before any validation and without a length bound, so a server or client that copies an untrusted header value into a Headers object can be stalled by a value such as "a" + N tabs + "\ta". The 5.19.1 fix removes the trailing regex and trims with an explicit character loop (CWE-1333; the CNA record labels it CWE-20).

entry_point.description: An attacker-supplied header value reaches a Headers object through Headers.append() or Headers.set() (directly or via fetch()/Request/Response header conversion). The surface is wider than "application passes untrusted input": undici's own fetch implementation feeds server-controlled header values into Headers.append from lib/fetch/index.js onHeaders (~1980-1996) and onUpgrade (~2080-2087), so a malicious origin can trigger the ReDoS in the client process without the application forwarding anything.

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on the defect, the <5.19.1 range and CVSS 3.1 7.5 High. They disagree on the weakness class: the CNA record and OSV use CWE-20 while NVD Primary uses CWE-1333 (Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity); both are recorded in cwe_ids.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read headerValueNormalize() at v5.19.0 and confirm the trailing regex alternative is the quadratic part and that append()/set() reach it before validation.
An independent reviewer must confirm f2324e54 is not an ancestor of v5.19.0 and is contained in v5.19.1.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range and record the CWE-20 vs CWE-1333 split.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
independent_corrections_accepted: Line precision: line 27 is the vulnerable `replace(` statement and line 28 carries the regex literal; the dataset keeps line 27 as the statement line.
CWE: CNA/OSV use CWE-20 while NVD Primary and GHSA use CWE-1333; CWE-1333 is the precise class and both are retained in cwe_ids.
Attacker surface: undici fetch itself routes response and upgrade headers into Headers.append, so the issue is reachable in a client without application forwarding; recorded in the entry point.
Duplicate check: the same v5.19.1 also fixes GHSA-5r9g-qh6m-jxff (CRLF injection in lib/core/request.js, a2eff054) — a different root cause, not a duplicate.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No JavaScript runtime or HTTP workload was executed; the complexity argument is static and no measured stall time is claimed.
The vulnerable path requires an application that copies untrusted header values into a Headers object; plain use of undici with trusted request headers is not affected.
The 5.19.1 fix still applies one anchored regex to the head of the string; the dossier does not claim that path is vulnerable.

The upstream advisory says "when untrusted values are passed into the functions"; the independent reviewer found a stronger direct path (undici fetch response/upgrade headers). This widens the attack surface but does not change the root cause.
open_questions: Whether every fetch()/Request/Response header path funnels through append()/set() without an earlier length check was not exhaustively audited.
